matchedRecords.name: Lewey Lake and Miami River public launch/turnaround anchors
matchedRecords.method: NYSDEC publishes the Lewey Lake Campground public launch, shallow-launch warning, seasonal operation, parking capacity, and camping facilities. Experience Our Adirondacks identifies the Miami River as accessed from the south end of Lewey Lake and passable approximately one mile upstream; the current Hamilton County paddling guide publishes a five-mile out-and-back route and a substantial-beaver-dam turnaround. The campground coordinate is the authoritative water-entry/return anchor; the Miami turnaround is an area objective, not a public take-out.

matchedRecords.name: New York Catskill Creek Kiwanis Park to Dutchman’s Landing public tidal access
matchedRecords.method: The official NYSDEC Hudson River Estuary access directory identifies Kiwanis Park/Catskill Creek as a municipal hand launch with six-car parking and Dutchman’s Landing as a municipal concrete launch at the mouth of Catskill Creek. Current regional tourism and school-district material corroborate the Catskill Middle School/West Main hand-launch area, while current launch guidance describes Dutchman’s Landing as a public ramp. Retain both as park-area water-entry controls and require field confirmation of school/park public-use boundaries, carry, parking, tide, and the wetted edge.

aliases: West Main Street Catskill Creek access

controls.name: Dutchman’s Landing Catskill Creek mouth launch
controls.coordinateText: NYSDEC lists Dutchman’s Landing as a municipal concrete launch at the mouth of Catskill Creek; current launch guidance corroborates the public ramp and coordinate. Confirm current operations, closures, parking, tide, ramp traffic, and legal carry.

matchedRecords.name: Delaware Blackbird Creek Reserve to The Rocks access anchors
matchedRecords.method: DNREC directly identifies the Blackbird Creek Reserve canoe/kayak launch, while the DNERR management plan identifies The Rocks as a downstream Fish & Wildlife boat-launch property. Coordinates are practical near-water access anchors corroborated by public mapping context; verify carry, wetted edge, gate, parking, CAP, landing, and current closure status in the field.
